properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 5 at 8:53PM EDT until October 5 at 11:15PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
FFWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Gadsden County in Big Bend Florida...
North Central Leon County in Big Bend Florida...

* Until 1115 PM EDT.

* At 853 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 6 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Tallahassee, Havana, Midway, Quincy, Gretna, Scotland, Freemont,
Florence, Shady Rest, Gibson, Littman, Hinson, Jamieson,
Branchville, Concord, Dogtown, Quincy Airport, Santa Clara, Orchard
Pond and Darsey.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...From 6 AM CDT Tuesday through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

Somerset, and Northern Piscataquis Counties.
